title: Notes screen swipe-delete has no undo, unlike a destructive action should
description: Deleting a note is immediate and permanent after the confirm dialog: onDismissed calls notifier.deleteNote(note.id) with no SnackBar/undo. Notes contain user-authored text (the most irreplaceable content in the app, unlike bookmarks which can be re-added trivially), yet there is no recovery path if the confirm is mis-tapped.
impact: Accidental deletion of a written note is unrecoverable. The confirm dialog reduces but does not eliminate fat-finger loss, and offers no second chance.
recommendation: Show a SnackBar with an 'تراجع' action after deletion that restores the note via addNote(...), and only finalize removal after the SnackBar times out.
evidence: onDismissed: (_) => notifier.deleteNote(note.id),  // no SnackBar, no undo

verdict.reasoning: Verified in notes_screen.dart: onDismissed (line 59) calls notifier.deleteNote(note.id) with no ScaffoldMessenger/SnackBar/undo anywhere in the file. deleteNote (bookmark_provider.dart:136-140) is a hard delete — it filters the note from state and persists via _dataSource.saveNotes, with no trash/soft-delete buffer, so deletion is genuinely permanent. Notes hold user-authored text, which is irreplaceable, and addNote (bookmark_provider.dart:98) exists, so an undo path is feasible. So far the claim is accurate. However, the claim materially overstates impact: lines 46-58 contain a confirmDismiss AlertDialog requiring an explicit "حذف" tap before onDismissed fires. Deletion therefore requires a deliberate swipe PLUS confirming a dialog — not a single mis-tap. The claim's "if the confirm is mis-tapped / no recovery path" framing ignores that the confirmation dialog IS the recovery affordance. In Material/Flutter idiom, a confirm dialog and an undo SnackBar are recognized alternatives for destructive actions, not a required pair. With a mandatory confirmation already guarding the action, an additional undo is a nice-to-have polish, not a medium-severity defect — hence downgraded to low.

title: Note sheet save button disabled-state is invisible: empty note silently no-ops with no feedback
description: The save FilledButton is always enabled-looking, but onPressed only calls onSave + pop when text.trim() is non-empty. With an empty field, tapping 'حفظ' does nothing and the sheet stays open with no error, hint, or button-disabled affordance. There is also no explicit cancel/close control, so the only exit for an empty note is dragging the sheet down.
impact: User taps 'حفظ' on an empty note and gets no response, appearing as a frozen/broken button. Editing an existing note and clearing it to empty also silently refuses to save (and cannot delete the note from here).
recommendation: Disable the button (onPressed: null) when the trimmed text is empty using a controller listener, or show a 'لا يمكن حفظ ملاحظة فارغة' message; add a close affordance and an explicit delete path when editing.
evidence: onPressed: () { final text = _controller.text.trim(); if (text.isNotEmpty) { widget.onSave(text); Navigator.pop(context); } },  // empty => no-op, button still looks active

verdict.reasoning:
The core mechanic is real: at note_sheet.dart:75-89 the FilledButton's onPressed is never null (always looks enabled with amber backgroundColor 0xFFD97706), and lines 76-82 only call onSave + pop when _controller.text.trim().isNotEmpty. So an empty/whitespace note silently no-ops with no SnackBar, no error text, and no disabled-button affordance. That part of the claim is accurate and code-grounded.

However, the claim is partly FALSE on its own evidence. It states 'There is also no explicit cancel/close control, so the only exit for an empty note is dragging the sheet down.' This is wrong: NoteSheet wraps its content in BaseBottomSheet, whose header (base_bottom_sheet.dart:72-75) renders an IconButton(Icons.close) that pops the sheet. Every BaseBottomSheet, including this one, has a visible X close affordance. So the user has a clear, explicit exit; the 'drag down only' assertion is false.

Severity is overstated at medium. Impact is minimal: the user must deliberately attempt to save an empty note (the field has an autofocus hint 'اكتب ملاحظتك...'), nothing destructive happens, and a close button plus drag-to-dismiss both exist. The added recommendation about a 'delete path when editing' is scope creep, not a flaw. This is a minor polish gap (no disabled-state/feedback on empty save), hence low severity.

title: Mushaf page-jump and navigation dialogs leak TextEditingControllers (never disposed)
description: _showPageJumpDialog() creates `final controller = TextEditingController(text: '$_currentPage');` inside the builder but never disposes it. Each time the user opens the page-jump dialog a new controller is allocated and abandoned. The thematic create-plan and khatmah create dialogs share this pattern (nameController never disposed).
impact: Minor but repeatable memory/resource leak each time these dialogs are opened; flagged by Flutter's own controller-disposal guidance and accumulates over a long reading session.
recommendation: Use a StatefulWidget dialog (or StatefulBuilder with a controller created in initState) and dispose the controller, or reuse a single controller owned by the screen state.
evidence: void _showPageJumpDialog() { final controller = TextEditingController(text: '$_currentPage'); showDialog(...); }  // never disposed

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed at the cited location. mushaf_view.dart:58-59 defines `void _showPageJumpDialog() { final controller = TextEditingController(text: '$_currentPage'); ... }` as a method-local variable wired to the dialog's TextField (line 66). There is no dispose() for it anywhere; the dialog closes via Navigator.pop (lines 78, 84, 92) leaving the controller abandoned. TextEditingController is a ChangeNotifier and should be disposed, so each open of the page-jump dialog leaks one. The "shared pattern" note is mixed: khatmah_screen.dart:18 (nameController, local, never disposed) genuinely matches, and the memorization screen (lines 100/112) is actually worse (new controller created inline inside build, leaking per rebuild) — but the claim's mention of a thematic create-plan dialog is inaccurate (the thematic feature contains no TextEditingController at all). That inaccuracy is only in the secondary "also affects" remark, not the cited primary location. Impact is genuinely minor: the leaked object is small and allocated only per dialog-open (not per frame in mushaf_view), the analyzer does not flag local-variable controllers by default, and Flutter idiom for short-lived dialogs often tolerates this. Low severity is appropriate.

title: Khatmah empty-state CTA is missing even though EmptyStateWidget supports one
description: EmptyStateWidget accepts actionLabel/onAction to render a primary button, but the khatmah empty state passes neither. The only way to create the first plan is the FloatingActionButton in the corner. New users see 'أنشئ خطة لختم القرآن الكريم' with no actionable button in the center where their attention is.

recommendation: Pass actionLabel: 'خطة جديدة', onAction: _showCreateDialog to the EmptyStateWidget so the empty state itself launches plan creation.
evidence: const EmptyStateWidget(icon: Icons.calendar_month_outlined, title: 'لا توجد خطط ختمة', description: 'أنشئ خطة لختم القرآن الكريم')  // no actionLabel/onAction

verdict.reasoning: Verified directly against the code. EmptyStateWidget (lib/core/widgets/empty_state_widget.dart lines 7-8, 15-16) declares optional actionLabel/onAction and renders a FilledButton CTA only when both are non-null (lines 50-56). The khatmah empty state (khatmah_screen.dart lines 193-198) constructs EmptyStateWidget with only icon/title/description and passes neither actionLabel nor onAction, so no center button renders. However the impact is genuinely minor — the FAB is clearly labeled 'خطة جديدة' with an add icon and invokes the exact same _showCreateDialog, so creation is discoverable; the missing center CTA is a polish/best-practice enhancement, not a functional or confusing defect. title: Tafsir in-sheet search does not dismiss keyboard and clearing query does not reset on chip change
description: Switching tafsir source via _selectTafsir() changes the content but leaves _inSheetQuery and the search field populated, so highlight markers from the previous tafsir's search persist (and may match nothing in the new text with no feedback). onSubmitted sets _inSheetQuery but never unfocuses, so on small screens the keyboard covers the freshly highlighted matches the user just searched for.
impact: After searching inside one tafsir and switching sources, stale highlight state lingers; and immediately after a search the keyboard hides the matched text the user wanted to read.
recommendation: Clear/_inSheetQuery and the controller (or re-run the search) when the tafsir source changes, and call FocusScope.unfocus() on submit so results are visible.
evidence: void _selectTafsir(int id) { setState(() => _selectedTafsirId = id); ... }  // _inSheetQuery left untouched; onSubmitted: (v) => setState(() => _inSheetQuery = v.trim()) // no unfocus

verdict.reasoning: Both described behaviors genuinely exist in lib/features/reader/widgets/tafsir_sheet.dart. (1) _selectTafsir() at lines 43-46 only updates _selectedTafsirId and persists it via setDefaultTafsirId; it never resets _inSheetQuery (line 29) or _searchController (line 28). When the tafsir source changes, the provider re-fetches new content (lines 85-87) and _highlightedTextSpan(plain, _inSheetQuery, ...) at lines 216-217 re-applies the stale query to the new text, so highlights persist and may match nothing in the new tafsir with no 'no matches' feedback; the search field also still shows the old query. (2) onSubmitted at line 141 is `(v) => setState(() => _inSheetQuery = v.trim())` with no FocusScope.unfocus(), so the keyboard stays up over the scrollable results in this bottom sheet (Flexible content, line 145) with no auto-scroll to the match. Note line 140 onChanged only setState({}) to toggle the clear button and does NOT update _inSheetQuery, so highlighting fires only on submit — which makes a committed query lingering across chip changes a realistic scenario, reinforcing the claim. Impact is minor (manual keyboard dismiss available; content is scrollable; stale highlight is confusing not broken), so low severity is correct. Line citations (43-46 and 124-142) are exact.

title: Audio bar slider is interactive and seekable before a track is loaded, with no track identity
description: The Slider's onChanged always calls seekToPercent(value) regardless of audioState.isLoading or whether duration is known. While loading (duration unknown) the user can still drag the thumb and issue seeks against an undefined duration. There is also no surah/verse/reciter label, so a user who scrolled away cannot tell what is playing before deciding to seek.
impact: Dragging the progress bar during load produces meaningless seeks; combined with no track identity, the audio control offers ambiguous, error-prone interaction during the most common race (tap play, then immediately try to scrub).
recommendation: Set Slider.onChanged to null while audioState.isLoading or duration<=0, and show the current surah/verse (+reciter) above the controls.
evidence: Slider(value: audioState.progress, onChanged: (value) { ref.read(audioProvider.notifier).seekToPercent(value); })  // no isLoading guard

verdict.reasoning: Both factual assertions hold against the actual code. (1) In lib/features/reader/widgets/audio_player_bar.dart lines 45-50 the Slider's onChanged unconditionally calls ref.read(audioProvider.notifier).seekToPercent(value) with NO guard on audioState.isLoading or duration. isLoading is set true while just_audio is loading/buffering (audio_provider.dart lines 104-107), and duration arrives asynchronously via durationStream (lines 111-115), so the thumb is draggable before duration is known. (2) No surah/verse/reciter label exists: the widget renders only the slider, position/duration text, and control buttons. The state holds currentChapterId and currentVerseKey (audio_provider.dart lines 14-15) but they are never displayed, and AudioPlayerBar is the only audio UI on the reader screen (reader_screen.dart lines 516, 552) so there is no adjacent label either. Caveat lowering impact: the 'seek against undefined duration' is functionally harmless, not a crash — seekToPercent computes targetMs = duration.inMilliseconds(0) * percent = 0 (audio_provider.dart lines 259-262), so a drag while loading just seeks to Duration.zero (a no-op to the start). The real, valid issue is the missing track identity, a genuine UX gap. Net: claim is real and correctly anchored; low severity is appropriate since neither sub-issue is harmful or high-impact.

title: No-network / search-error state offers a generic message but no retry on Home search
description: When the search provider errors (e.g. offline and FTS unavailable, or API failure), _buildSearchSlivers renders a static 'تعذر تنفيذ البحث. حاول مرة أخرى.' text with no retry button and no way to re-issue the query other than editing the field and pressing submit again. The chapter-list error path does provide an onRetry, so this is an inconsistency that leaves the search flow without a recovery affordance.
impact: After a failed search the user has a dead message and must manually re-trigger; there is no one-tap retry, unlike the rest of the app's error states.
recommendation: Add a retry action (ref.invalidate(quranSearchProvider(_submittedQuery))) to the search error sliver, matching the chapter-list AppErrorWidget pattern.
evidence: error: (error, _) => [ SliverToBoxAdapter(child: ... Text('تعذر تنفيذ البحث. حاول مرة أخرى.') ) ]  // no onRetry

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed. In lib/features/home/screens/home_screen.dart, _buildSearchSlivers' error branch (lines 289-301) renders a static Text('تعذر تنفيذ البحث. حاول مرة أخرى.') inside SliverToBoxAdapter>Padding>Center with no button, InkWell, onTap, or ref.invalidate. The text says "try again" but provides no control to do so. By contrast the chapter-list error path (lines 193-196) uses AppErrorWidget with onRetry: ()=>ref.invalidate(chaptersProvider), and AppErrorWidget (error_widget.dart lines 34-41) renders a FilledButton labeled 'إعادة المحاولة' when onRetry!=null — so the same screen is inconsistent. The recommendation is valid: quranSearchProvider is a FutureProvider.family<..,String>, so ref.invalidate(quranSearchProvider(_submittedQuery)) would re-run it. Worse, re-submitting the identical query via onSubmitted only setState(()=>_submittedQuery=value) with an unchanged value, so Riverpod returns the cached error rather than retrying — the field is no reliable recovery for the same query; the user must edit the text. Still low severity: search is a secondary feature, failures are typically transient network, and the field remains visible so the user is not hard-stuck. No Directionality/theme wrapper mitigates this; it is purely a missing affordance.
